Development guide

Tech Radar

Seventy-two products and tools, grouped by the job they do in an agent stack; OpenRouter appears in two groups. Each group explains what that type of product is for, then lists the options with what each one does, how it is supplied, and its current status.

A note on Tech Radar

This page is still a draft and may not reflect the latest technologies or releases.

The entries are based on published documentation, not local deployment tests. Carry out your own research before adopting any option.

Key points

  • Start with the job you need done, then compare the options inside that group.
  • Scope is AWS; managed Claude or OpenAI through Bedrock is the default route, with direct APIs as exceptions.
  • Versions are dated 17 November 2026, except the Persistent agents category, dated 19 November 2026, and the LLM model, coding tool and provider tables in Models and model access, dated 20 November 2026. Command-line tools and SDKs ship weekly, so confirm the current version before adoption.

How to read this radar

Each group below opens with a short description of what that type of product is and when to use it, then a table of the products in the group. The table says what each product does, how it is supplied, and its status. Do not use is reserved for products that are officially winding down, retired, closed to new customers, or at end of support. The linked Tech Scan page gives the safer route, or the wind-down, closure or retirement date. A product that is usable only if you meet a stated condition keeps its Available or Emerging label and carries a Conditions apply flag beside it — always read the condition in its entry before adopting. Hold is now only for products that are dormant or stalled, never for a product that is merely conditional.

Labels on this page

Available
Generally available or actively maintained, and usable from this reference.
Emerging
In preview, early access, new and still settling, or not yet proven for this route. Prove it on representative work before adoption.
Conditions apply
Not a status on its own: it sits beside an Available or Emerging label and means the entry states a condition to meet before adopting, such as a pinned version, a licence check or a named limitation. Always read the condition.
Hold
Only for a product that is dormant or stalled, with no official wind-down: no release or commit for months. Confirm it is still maintained before adopting.
Do not use
Do not adopt from this reference: officially winding down, retired, closed to new customers, or at end of support.

Versions are dated 17 November 2026, except the Persistent agents category, dated 19 November 2026, and the LLM model, coding tool and provider tables in Models and model access, dated 20 November 2026; a version that moves weekly will be out of date soon after that; the Sources list gives the vendor page or repository where the current version can be confirmed.

Check before adoption

  • Exact product, version, endpoint, model or inference profile, and region
  • Licence and hosting, including where data travels and whether the region you need is supported
  • Fast-moving command-line tools and SDKs pinned to an exact version, not tracking latest
  • Retired, winding-down and closed-to-new-customers products excluded, with the replacement or the closure date named in the linked reference
  • Route proved on representative work, with failures retained, before wider adoption

Models and model access

This category has four groups. LLM models generate text and code. Agentic coding tools are clients that put models to work in a repository. A model service or provider gives access to many models through one platform. Decision models return a choice or probability for a defined question.

Product notes

For LiteLLM, pin a checked release and verify its digests before adoption: versions 1.82.7 and 1.82.8 (March 2026) and 1.107.0 (21 October 2026) were malicious. [64][65][66][67] OpenRouter has been part of Stripe since 10 November 2026 (US time). [61] The Portkey open-source gateway has had no release since 12 January 2026, and Palo Alto Networks completed its acquisition of Portkey on 29 May 2026. [27][75] Envoy AI Gateway was renamed Agent Router; the Agentic AI Foundation dated that announcement 9 September 2026. Use 1.2.1 or later. Version 1.2.1 fixes a high-severity advisory, scored 8.1, in which the MCP proxy could be reached on every network interface and its trusted headers bypassed (GHSA-mgwh-j6v5-5mf8). MCP, the Model Context Protocol, is a standard way for an agent to call tools. [29][62][63] Unkey is source-available under the FSL-1.1-ALv2 licence; check that the licence fits your use before adopting it. [30] CISA lists four LiteLLM vulnerabilities as exploited in 2026, and attackers’ agents search for exposed proxies with default master keys. Do not expose the proxy or its admin interface to the internet, replace the default master key, and rotate provider keys after any exposure. [76][77][78] Kong published five high-severity AI Gateway advisories on 10 November 2026; use 2.2.1 or later, and 2.3.1 for the SAML audience fix on the 2.3 line. [82][83][84][85][86] Its hosted successor, Prisma AIRS AI Gateway, is proprietary and is listed for the Americas region; it is not a Singapore-region route today. [89][90]

Context and memory

Context is the information supplied to a model for a task. Retrieval finds information in sources; memory retains information, such as past sessions or preferences, for later use.

Product notes

The AWS-first route is the Managed Knowledge Base, generally available on 17 June 2026, with AgentCore Memory beside it.

When bringing your own vector store, consider OpenSearch Serverless for scale and hybrid search, or Aurora with pgvector for data already in PostgreSQL. Aurora’s extension list now includes pgvector up to 0.8.2, depending on the engine version. [56] Zep Community Edition is retired: it was deprecated on 2 April 2025, so do not adopt it. [17][21]

Harness and agent frameworks

Product notes

AgentCore Harness is the managed form of that loop: it is defined by configuration, powered by Strands, and generally available since June 2026. AgentCore Runtime is different: it hosts agent code you write yourself. For explicit control of the loop in Python or TypeScript, consider the code-level frameworks in the table. [18]

Microsoft Agent Framework reached 1.0 on 3 April 2026 and is the successor to AutoGen, which is archived. AG2 is a separate community fork of AutoGen, not Microsoft’s product. [34] Thoughtworks moved LangGraph from Adopt to Trial in April 2026 and said it is no longer the default choice for every agent system. That blip is not on the current edition. [70] The OpenAI Agents SDK is still at 0.25.0, before 1.0. A closed April 2026 issue plans to mark 1.0 Production/Stable, and that release has not shipped. [73] Pin 1.26.0 or a later checked release, and do not install the PyPI releases 1.26.1 or 1.26.2: they were a malicious credential stealer published on 18 November 2026 (UTC+8). PyPI’s newest release after those versions were removed is the clean 1.26.0. If either malicious release was installed anywhere, treat every secret reachable from that host as exposed. [79][80][81][91]

Persistent agents

A persistent agent owns an ongoing responsibility rather than one task. It keeps memory between runs, can start work on a schedule or after an event, and may start other agent sessions. Its name or separate chat is not an access boundary: check whose identity, secrets and computer it uses.

Product notes

Devin Bots use their own connections and secrets; before a Bot uses one of your sign-ins or secrets, an approval card says what approving will share. Everyone who can use a shared Bot can read its memory. [92] [93]

Kiro Crew workers share the bot’s memory and workspace and inherit its approval mode. New bots start in Trust mode, which acts without per-action approval, so set Normal or Reads before a trial. [94] [95]

OpenAI dots act through the owner’s connected apps and existing permissions, with built-in approval rules and Custom Rules. [96] [97]

Cue by Manus gives each agent its own email, phone number, wallet and computer; purchases are made within a budget the user sets and confirmed by the user, and Cue is in early access with an invitation code. [102] [103]

Muse is a consumer product for people 18 and over in the United States. It asks before important actions such as sending email or making a purchase, and its permission authority is separate from the agent. [104] [105]

Hermes Agent’s default smart approval mode lets a second model judge whether a dangerous command is safe; set manual approval before it handles work data. Cron jobs deny dangerous commands by default, and YOLO mode turns approval prompts off for a session. [110] [108] [109] [111]

OpenClaw supports one trust boundary per gateway: a single operator or a team whose members trust each other. For mutually adversarial users, its security documentation recommends separate gateways and credentials, ideally separate OS users or hosts. [106] [107]

Every Grok Bot on an account shares one cloud computer, its files and its browser sign-ins, so separate Bots are not a security boundary. A Team Bot gives everyone one set of apps and secrets, and approval cards raised by background work expire after 30 minutes. [98] [99] [100] [101]

Product notes

AgentCore Evaluations scores agent behaviour using 15 built-in evaluators and reads OpenTelemetry traces, a standard record of each step the agent took. Bedrock Guardrails Automated Reasoning checks a response against formal-logic rules, but only in detect-only mode (it reports a problem but does not block the response): it returns findings and your application decides what to do. Amazon CodeGuru Reviewer has been closed to new customers since 7 November 2025, because new repository associations stopped on that date. Existing associations can carry on for now. [14][15][16]

Sandbox and execution

A sandbox restricts where code runs and what it can access, according to its configuration. Isolation alone does not deny access to credentials, the network or the host; configure identity and outgoing network controls separately. A microVM is a small virtual machine that can isolate a workload.

ProductLambda MicroVMsWhat it doesServerless compute primitive inside Lambda: a dedicated, stateful Firecracker microVM (a small virtual machine that isolates one workload) per user, session or job, snapshot-launched, with its own HTTPS endpoint and run, suspend, resume and terminate lifecycle.TypeAWS managed serviceStatusAvailableVersionService; GA 22 Jun 2026; Singapore from 19 Aug 2026; 14 regions from 22 Oct 2026; x86 from 11 Nov 2026EvidenceSandbox

Product notes

Nitro Sandboxes, launched on 9 November 2026, give each EKS pod, ECS task or EC2 workload its own hardware-isolated microVM. Nitro Enclaves are a different boundary: they protect sensitive data from the parent instance and are not a general-purpose sandbox for untrusted agent code. [12]

Lambda MicroVMs are a serverless form of the same idea, generally available since 22 June 2026. They have been in Asia Pacific (Singapore) since 19 August 2026, and in 14 regions since 22 October 2026. Arm (AWS Graviton) is the default architecture. x86 has been available since 11 November 2026 in every region except Asia Pacific (Hong Kong), Asia Pacific (Malaysia), Asia Pacific (Thailand) and Europe (Spain). [22][57][59][58] E2B is the hosted alternative, with an open-source runtime. A comparison published by Lizard, which sells a competing sandbox, measured 1,200 sandbox starts (300 from one runner in US East for each of four products) and reported median create-to-first-command times of 264 ms for E2B, 819 ms for Daytona and 929 ms for Modal, and 228 ms for Lizard’s own product. [23][68]

Software factories

In this guide, a software factory connects development tasks, agent work and checks into a repeatable delivery workflow. It can coordinate local tools or cloud agents, with work submitted for review.

[42][43][60][44][45] On the same Terminal-Bench 2.1 leaderboard, GPT 5.5 scored 57.30% in the Factory harness, the same score as in Codex. [71]

AI workflow skill packs

Skill packs are collections of reusable instructions or procedures for coding agents. They guide workflows such as planning, building, verifying and reviewing work. Pin a pack to a reviewed version or commit before adoption, and check its licence and instructions.

Product notes

The packs differ in shape, so their counts are not comparable: Superpowers is a methodology that triggers itself, pstack is a Cursor-first set of playbooks entered by command, gstack organises the agent as a team of roles, and tstack covers the pull-request lifecycle. Pin a pack to a reviewed version or commit before adopting it, and check its licence: ub-mode is now MIT-licensed, but its final rule tells the agent to push to the main line. [52]
